items.reason: The gap does not exist in the tree: neither agent-dispatch.yml nor autofix.yml interpolates any ${{ }} into a run: step — every untrusted value already travels via env: — and it is enforced by the blocking run-injection/script-injection rules in scripts/security/check-actions.mjs (npm run security:actions, ci.yml) plus a whole-tree fixture and a pinned per-job permissions map in scripts/review/__tests__/gate-check.test.mjs (npm run test:review, ci.yml + release.yml), so I changed nothing rather than edit files to satisfy a scanner.

Added docs/architecture/candidate-data-flow.md — one CV upload traced hop by hop (route -> temp workdir -> spawned Python -> model provider -> SQLite -> cleanup), the tables candidate data comes to rest in, the copies that are not the database, a per-adapter egress table, the two egress seals, and four named gaps — and wired it so it cannot rot silently: a new entry in scripts/docs/feature-doc-map.json couples the 13 source paths it traces to it (Stop hook), and ADR 0005 cites it under sources: so npm run docs:check fails if it is deleted or moved.

Needs a shell: the repo already ships scripts/perf/check-budget.mjs and docs/development/performance-budget.md, and both say the only two missing steps are `node scripts/perf/check-budget.mjs --record` (which MEASURES the module graph and writes perf-budget.json) and adding `- run: npm run perf:budget` to the node-quality job in ci.yml. I cannot execute anything, and hand-writing ceilings I have not measured would produce exactly the budget the tool's own header warns about — one that either fails honest work or passes everything — so I left it uncalibrated rather than fake the numbers.

Added app/_lib/db/rollback-drill.test.ts, which rehearses the runbook in docs/architecture/releases.md on every push (npm run test:unit = the node-tests job in ci.yml and the gate job in release.yml, so a tag cannot publish a version whose rollback has not just been executed): it pins the v0.1.x column shape and fails on any migration that drops/renames a column or adds a NOT NULL without a DEFAULT, and it runs the real dump -> bad upgrade -> restore cycle through scripts/db-dump.mjs / db-load.mjs asserting the workspace comes back byte-identical and that a load without --replace refuses AND writes nothing. releases.md now documents the drill and answers the down-step question explicitly (there are none; the dump is the reverse, by ADR 0002).

lessons: Check this repo's existing gates before writing anything: it already enforces far more than a scanner can see from the outside (scripts/security/check-actions.mjs blocks ${{ }} in run: as a BLOCKING CI rule, scripts/review/__tests__/gate-check.test.mjs pins each untrusted-input workflow's exact permissions map, scripts/docs/check-adrs.mjs fails when an ADR's sources: path vanishes). Two of four dispatched items were about practices that were already operating or already scaffolded.

The repo's own convention is that a doc is only trusted when something re-reads it: scripts/docs/feature-doc-map.json couples source globs to the doc that describes them and a Stop hook enforces it, and ADR sources: are existence-checked by npm run docs:check. A new architecture doc that is not registered in at least one of those is drift waiting to happen — register it in the same change.

Ascent items about 'nothing fails when X regresses' are often already half-built here and blocked on one CALIBRATION run (scripts/perf/check-budget.mjs ships with no perf-budget.json because it was written in a sandbox with no execution). An agent with no shell cannot finish those; the honest move is to name the exact two commands rather than invent baseline numbers.
